newsitem.title: FRANCE: IBM, Gemplus in 'smart card' agreement.
newsitem.headline: IBM, Gemplus in 'smart card' agreement.

text.p: IBM Corp and French firm Gemplus, which makes so-called 'smart cards' in which a computer chip is incorporated onto a plastic card, signed a commercial agreement on Thursday to expand their activities in the market for chip-encoded cards which is expected to boom.
The industry expects three billion chip-encoded cards to be in circulation by the year 2000 serving the telecommunications, banking, airline, insurance and health markets.
"The market will grow from a billion dollars currently to 20 billion toward the year 2000," Peter Sany, managing director of IBM's Smart Card Solutions division, told a news conference.

Gemplus chairman and founder Marc Lassus said the accord envisaged technical cooperation with the aim of developing new products. The deal will not involve any exchange of shares or stakes and it is not exclusive in nature, Sany said.
Privately-held Gemplus is controlled by several French and international investors, including GE Capital.
